problem:

A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $Σ$ shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the matrices $U$ and $V?$

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $Σ$ shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the matrices $U$ and $V?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's find the singular value decomposition of $A$ using the usual algorithm.

- **Step 1.** Compute ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 5 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}18 & -6 \\ -6 & 34\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step 2.** Find the singular values: From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that ${\sigma }_{1}=6$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=4.$

- **Step 3.** Find the right singular vectors of $A$ (i.e., the unit eigenvectors of ${A}^{T}\,A$):

- For ${\lambda }_{1}={\sigma }_{1}^{2}=36,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-36I & =[\begin{aligned}18 & -6 \\ -6 & 34\end{aligned}]-36[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-18 & -6 \\ -6 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-36I)v=0$ gives a unit eigenvector

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}={\sigma }_{2}^{2}=16,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-16I & =[\begin{aligned}18 & -6 \\ -6 & 34\end{aligned}]-16[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 \\ -6 & 18\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-16I)v=0$ gives a unit eigenvector

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}].
$$

- **Step 4.** Find the left singular vectors of $A$: Since we know the singular values and right singular vectors, we can compute the columns of $U$ as follows:

- First, we compute ${u}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{1}}A{v}_{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}\frac{18}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{6}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- Then, we compute ${u}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{2} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{2}}A{v}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{12}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we construct the matrices $U$ and $V:$

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]
$$
